items.prompt: GET /audit-logs was correctly tenant-scoped, yet the dashboard leaked another tenant's audit rows. What lesson does the guide draw?
items.answer: Every reader of the table, the dashboard included, must apply the organization rule itself
distractors: The endpoint's scope should have been inherited by the dashboard through shared middleware
The leak came from a forged JWT, so token verification needed hardening rather than scoping
Dashboards are cached per role, so the leak came from a stale entry in that cache
items.explanation: Having one correctly scoped endpoint did not protect a second reader of the same array: the original dashboard returned store.auditLogs.slice(0, 25) unfiltered.

items.prompt: The store holds 26 Nova rows (newest) followed by 1 Acme row. A version of the dashboard slices the first 25 rows and THEN filters by organization. What does the Acme admin get?
items.answer: Zero rows - the owner's row silently disappears
distractors: Their one Acme row
One Acme row plus 24 Nova rows
25 Nova rows
items.explanation: Only filter-then-slice is correct; otherwise row order - which another tenant controls just by being busy - becomes an access rule. (The ORIGINAL code did not filter at all and leaked 25 Nova rows.)

items.prompt: Why does the fix export a single auditLogScope(actor) function instead of writing the role/organization comparison in each reader?
items.answer: Two copies of the rule are how the endpoints came to disagree
distractors: A named function is faster than an inline arrow, because V8 can inline it
The dedicated endpoint needed a different rule, so the check had to be parameterized
Express route handlers cannot contain inline filter callbacks over store arrays
items.explanation: Both visibleAuditLogs and services.auditLogs call one auditLogScope; audit-scope.test.ts pins the two readers together by asserting they return the same row ids for the same actor.

items.prompt: A LEARNER requests both the dashboard and GET /audit-logs. Why does visibleAuditLogs keep an explicit learner early return instead of relying on the predicate?
items.answer: The contracts differ: the dashboard returns [] with 200, the endpoint refuses with 403
distractors: The predicate would throw for learners, because a learner's organizationId is null
Learners have no organization, so the predicate alone would return every row in the store
The early return is a performance shortcut that has no effect on the response
items.explanation: Learner difference is deliberate and stays in each reader. The empty list also does not depend on the store being empty, so a learner cannot infer whether events exist.

items.prompt: The fix also changed the fixture's auditLogs from [] to one seeded row per tenant. Why was that necessary?
items.answer: With an empty fixture the leak cannot be observed
distractors: The dashboard crashed on an empty array, which hid the real bug
totalPages needs two rows
It replaces the agreement test
items.explanation: Ownership tests need data from more than one tenant; with no rows, every 'no foreign rows returned' assertion passes vacuously.

items.prompt: An admin is demoted to LEARNER while still holding an 8-hour token. What happens on their next request?
items.answer: They act as a LEARNER at once: only sub is trusted from the JWT, the role is re-read from the store
distractors: They keep admin rights until the token expires, because the role is a claim inside the JWT
The token is rejected on the next request, because its signature no longer matches the role
They keep admin rights until they log out and back in, which issues a token with the new role
items.explanation: Hop 4 of the trace: req.actor is built from the user row found by payload.sub, so role changes take effect on the next request.

items.prompt: Before the fix, the leaked Nova row was in the dashboard JSON. Why would a screenshot-based UI check never have caught it?
items.answer: The audit panel reads /audit-logs, not dashboard.auditLogs
distractors: The panel filtered out foreign rows on the client before rendering them
The leaked row only ever appeared in the platform admin's dashboard
The dashboard response was compressed and could not be inspected in a screenshot
items.explanation: Only a response-level assertion could find this bug - a reminder that API payloads are an attack surface even when the UI ignores a field.

items.prompt: A PLATFORM_ADMIN completes a lesson for an Acme learner. Can the Acme org admin see the resulting audit row?
items.answer: No: the row is stamped with actor.organizationId, which is null for a platform admin
distractors: Yes: the row is stamped with the course's organization, taken from the enrollment
Yes: rows written by a platform admin are visible to every tenant's admin
No: platform admins are blocked from completing other learners' lessons in the first place
items.explanation: The course fixed the READERS; this is the matching WRITER defect. Fix: use course.organizationId from enrollmentContext when calling audit.

items.prompt: toAppError picks the HTTP status by regex over the error message. What happens to publishing an already-published course ("Cannot publish course draft from PUBLISHED")?
items.answer: 403, because the message contains "cannot" - though it is really a 409 conflict
distractors: 409, because the regex recognises the word publish and maps it to a conflict
404, because a published course no longer has a draft that could be found
500, because the message matches none of the patterns in toAppError
items.explanation: Message text decides the contract, so rewording a message silently changes HTTP behavior. Throw typed errors and map by class, not text.

items.prompt: publishCourse returns 404 for an unknown id but 403 for another tenant's course. Why is that a problem?
items.answer: It lets a user confirm which ids exist in another tenant
distractors: It is not a problem: 403 correctly tells the caller they lack permission for that course
The 403 body leaks the course title
404s make safe retries impossible
items.explanation: The lookup runs before assertCanAuthorCourse. Resolve the resource within the actor's visible scope and return the same 404 when absent or foreign.

items.prompt: A learner double-clicks 'Issue certificate' three times on a completed enrollment. What ends up in the store?
distractors: One; later calls return it
One; later calls fail with 409
One row, because verificationId is unique per enrollment and later inserts fail
items.explanation: issueCertificate always pushes a new record with a fresh id("verify"); the fix returns the existing ISSUED certificate for the enrollment.

items.prompt: Porting visibleAuditLogs to Prisma, which version reproduces the ORIGINAL bug?
items.answer: findMany({ take: 25 }), then filter the array in JavaScript
distractors: findMany({ where: scope, take: 25 })
findMany({ where: scopeWhere(actor) }) followed by .slice(0, 25) in JavaScript
findMany({ where: { organizationId }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 25 })
items.explanation: The limit must apply after the scope, in the same query (take with where); limiting first and filtering in application code is the bug.

items.front: services.login compares plaintext passwords (services.ts:55) and JWT_SECRET defaults to "local-learning-secret" (config index.ts:6). Risk and fix?
items.back: Anyone can sign a token (e.g. sub user-platform) on a process started without the variable, and stored passwords are readable. Hash at seed time with bcrypt.compare at login, and make JWT_SECRET required outside development/test.

items.front: enroll (services.ts:163-172) never checks for an existing enrollment of the same learner and version. Effect and database-era fix?
items.back: Repeated calls create parallel enrollments with separate progress. In a database, add a unique constraint on (learnerId, courseVersionId) and return the existing enrollment on conflict.

items.front: Name three consequences of choosing HTTP status by regex over error messages (errors.ts:31-32).
items.back: Publish-from-PUBLISHED becomes 403 instead of 409; a lesson from another version is 403 instead of 400/422 (and a test pins it); an out-of-range quiz score matches nothing and becomes 500. Throw typed errors (ConflictError, ValidationError) and map by class.
